journald: add ability to filter known log messages Known log messages can be filtered out by passing journalctl the '--filter-known/-i' flag. journalctl will look for the database of known log message at the specified path (defaults to /var/log/known-messages.bin when none is provided). This is intended to make it easier for developers to find interesting log messages. BUG=chromium:930348 TEST=Added unit tests TEST=launch journalctl with '-i' flag and ensure known messages are filtered out Change-Id: Ie673337a0d806c51e7fb5191337e995cd8ad35bd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1461233 Commit-Ready: Christopher Morin <cmtm@google.com> Tested-by: Christopher Morin <cmtm@google.com> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org>

journald: fix dangling /dev/log symlink With the move to journald, the syslog socket at /dev/log has been replaced by a symlink pointing to /run/systemd/journal/dev-log. Certain processes using minijail bind mount /dev, but don't bind mount the symlink target, and so have a dangling symlink at /dev/log. Most processes using minijail use --mount-dev and mount /dev/log explicitly and so aren't affected by this. Mount /run/systemd/journal/ into the namespaces of processes that directly mount /dev. BUG=chromium:932761 TEST=Ensure log messages from affected processes can be seen in the journal TEST=Inspect the mount namespaces of all processes running on the system for any dangling symlinks at /dev/log Change-Id: I577e71540d8b78aad9672cc66f6825873689616d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1478386 Commit-Ready: Christopher Morin <cmtm@google.com> Tested-by: Christopher Morin <cmtm@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

video: Use longer timelimit for VDA tests This CL doubles the time limit for video tests that run video_decode_accelerator_unittest. This will fix their failures on daisy due to timeout. In addition, we will be able to get more informative messages when the tests fail due to other reasons. Currently, if the test failed on some test cases, the binary test will retry them to reduce flakiness. But, this retries sometimes cause timeout. In such case, the test is kileed and cannot report failed test cases. By this change, the test will be able to run to the end even if there are some failed test cases. BUG=chromium:932348 TEST=run video.DecodeAccelH264 on daisy Change-Id: I6c6e00baeb9ab442ad8ee6c4c31127a64af44a7b Signed-off-by: Keiichi Watanabe <keiichiw@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1477575 Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hirokazu Honda <hiroh@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org>

iteflash: add '-m' flag to config I2C MUX channel. This CL enables iteflash to config I2C MUX to choose EC channel without Servo/Dut-control. Iteflash in CCD mode used to have servo-independence since DragonEgg, but Octopus ITE boards now have I2C MUX, which needs to be configured. This is to keep this servo-indepence in CCD mode. BUG=b:123901082 BRANCH=none TEST=manually ran iteflash with or without -m on duts with ITE EC. [Ampton] (checked dut_i2c_mux is none.) $ ./build/ampton/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -e -w ${IMG} failed $ ./build/ampton/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -r ${IMG_READ} failed $ ./build/ampton/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -e -w ${IMG} -m $ ./build/ampton/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -r ${IMG_READ} -m [Bip] (checked dut_i2c_mux is none.) $ ./build/bip/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -e -w ${IMG} failed $ ./build/bip/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -r ${IMG_READ} failed $ ./build/ampton/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -e -w ${IMG} -m $ ./build/ampton/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -r ${IMG_READ} -m [DragonEgg] $ ./build/dragonegg/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -e -w ${IMG} $ ./build/dragonegg/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -r ${IMG_READ} $ ./build/dragonegg/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -e -w ${IMG} -m failed $ ./build/dragonegg/util/iteflash -W 1 -c ccd -r ${IMG_READ} -m failed Change-Id: I9be14a350d32f7716c583b1e5d5b568c16d09dbf Signed-off-by: Namyoon Woo <namyoon@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1470782

vm_tools: Cicerone Fuzz Test Fuzz test for the Cicerone's ContainerListenerImpl. This is a boundary between the untrusted code in the container and the trusted VM code, so it's important that it be secure. It's not perfect; the fuzz test can't actually start another VM or Container even though it can exercise some of the parts.
